title: Lesson 5: BLESS - Share Your Story and the Gospel
description: The last BLESS rhythm. Someone told you the good news, and now you get to tell your one: their story, your story, and His story, with a simple picture you can draw on a napkin.

blocks.text: In Lessons 2 through 4 you prayed for your one, listened, shared a table, and served. You are blessed to be a blessing, and all of that has been building trust. Now comes the rhythm the others have been making room for: Story. You get to share the best thing that has ever happened to you.

blocks.alt: A man who had been blind from birth, with his eyes open after being healed by Jesus

blocks.title: I Was Blind, Now I See
blocks.text:
Jesus once met a man who had been blind from birth. After Jesus healed him, the religious leaders dragged him in for an interrogation. They wanted theology. They wanted answers. They wanted him to take their side against Jesus.

The man did not have a sermon ready. He did not have a polished argument. He simply told them what he knew.

"One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see." (John 9:25)

That is sharing your faith at its simplest. You do not have to be a theologian. You do not need every answer. You just need to tell someone honestly what Jesus has done in your life, and then point them to the One who can do it in theirs.
That is the heart of this rhythm. You tell what Jesus has done for you, and you point to the One who can do it for them. The rest of this lesson helps you do it.
Someone Told You

Before you ever tell your one about Jesus, remember how the good news reached you. Jesus came to make the Father known: "No one has ever seen God; the only God, who is at the Father's side, he has made him known" (John 1:18). Then He sent ordinary people to keep telling it. Somewhere along the way, someone told you. A parent, a friend, a pastor, maybe a stranger. Their feet carried the good news to you, and Paul says those feet are beautiful (Romans 10:15).
5.1 - Who first told you the good news about Jesus, and what did it mean to you?
When the Time Is Right

Story comes last in BLESS for a reason. When you have prayed for your one, listened, shared meals, and served, the conversation about Jesus has been on its way for a while. It no longer feels like a sales pitch. It feels like what friends talk about. And the Holy Spirit has been at work in you and in them long before this moment. You do not have to change anyone's heart. You carry, and Jesus heals.
But in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect.

Notice the word Peter chose. Always be prepared, not always be presenting, because preparation is the internal work that gets done long before any conversation. You shape your story and learn the gospel so that when the moment comes, when a friend asks why you seem different or when a coworker opens up about a hard season, you are ready, not polished, not perfect, just ready.
Three Stories

Every faith conversation has three stories on the table: their story, your story, and His story. Hold them in that order. You listen first, you share your own story briefly, and then you point to Jesus.

blocks.title: Your One's Story, Your Story, His Story
content: Your one's story. Start by listening. Through the BLESS rhythms you already know something of what they carry, what they hope for, and where they hurt. Ask, ask again, and remember. When you have heard them, what you say next lands in their real life instead of bouncing off.
Your story. Tell what Jesus has done for you, in about a minute. Like the man born blind, you do not need every answer, only what you know.
His story. Point to Jesus: His life, His death for our sins, and His resurrection. This is the story that can change theirs, and it is the one you will learn to draw below.

blocks.text: Look again at the man in John 9. When the leaders questioned him, he told his story plainly. Later Jesus found him and showed him who He was, and the man said, "Lord, I believe" (John 9:38). Your story opens the door. His story is the one that saves.
Your Story: Keep It Short
Your story is a short bridge into His story, not the whole conversation. Keep it simple: "There was a time when ____, but then I met Jesus and discovered ____, and now I ____."
5.2 - Write one short testimony using that frame. Keep it plain enough to say in about one minute.
His Story: The 3 Circles

There will come a moment when your one needs more than your story. They need His. For that you need something simple enough to draw on a napkin, clear enough that you do not stumble, and easy enough that your one could share it with someone else. The 3 Circles is that kind of picture. Step through it below.

God's design is a good world and a close relationship with Him. Sin and brokenness came when people went their own way, and the squiggly arrows show how people try to escape: money, success, relationships, distractions. The gospel is that God did not leave us stuck. He sent His Son Jesus, who lived without sin, died on the cross to pay for sin, and rose again on the third day.

For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures.

The way back is not earning but turning. Repent means to turn from going your own way, and believe means to trust Jesus as Savior and King. Then you recover and pursue God's design: He forgives you, makes you new, and restores you.
5.3 - Which part of the 3 Circles feels hardest to explain in your own words?
This Week's Practice
Most people never share the gospel because they do not feel ready. The way to feel ready is to practice with someone who already loves you, so the words are there when your one asks.

blocks.title: Practice Drawing the 3 Circles
content: Pick one person this week to walk through the 3 Circles with. A friend, a family member, or a trusted Christian works great as a first try.
Grab a napkin, a sheet of paper, or a whiteboard. Draw it as you talk, not before. Drawing as you go is what makes it feel natural.
Try all three stories: ask about their story, tell your one-minute story, then draw His.
End with a simple invitation: "Where do you see yourself on this picture? Where do you want to be? Is there anything keeping you from turning to Jesus today?"

blocks.text: 5.4 - Who will you practice the 3 Circles with this week, so you are ready for your one?
Lesson 5 Review

Like the man born blind, you do not need a sermon ready. You tell what Jesus has done for you and point to the One who can do it for your one. Every faith conversation holds three stories: your one's story, your story, and His story. Your job is to plant, and God gives the growth (1 Corinthians 3:6-7). That frees you from having to convince anyone, and it frees your one from feeling like a project.

That is BLESS: begin with prayer, listen, eat, serve, and story. God blessed Abram to be a blessing, and that blessing reached you. Your one is how it keeps moving. Each week, ask a Christian friend, and let them ask you: Who did you BLESS this week?
In the next lesson, you will carry the BLESS rhythms into your 2nd Space, the place where most of your week is spent.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?

The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson. The 3 Circles is adapted from the 3 Circles Life Conversation Guide from the North American Mission Board. The weekly question "Who did you BLESS this week?" comes from the KC Underground BLESS guide.
